course_name_en: Modeling and Simulation of Mechanical Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Prepare the mechanical engineer to know the current trends in the field of structure design.

Form competencies regarding the in-depth and multilateral analysis of both constructive solutions and the behavior of resistance structures, so that the mechanical engineer can make optimal design decisions for them.
Ensure specific competencies regarding the design of rational models of mechanical structures that comply with the criteria of minimum weight, durability, and maximum operational safety.

syllabus_topics: Resistance and Stability of Steel Structural Elements
Bars Subjected to Axial Compression Stability Calculation
Buckling of Compressed Bars: Influence of Support Conditions
Bars Subjected to Bending with Axial Force
Calculation of Resistance and Stability of Solid Web Girders
Laboratory: Analytical Calculation of Structures and their Global Analysis using the Finite Element Method
Laboratory: Analytical Calculation and Finite Element Analysis of Different Types of Joints Used in Metal Structures
Laboratory: Calculation and Construction of Metal Structures Specific to Transport Machines
Laboratory: Calculation and Construction of Metal Structures Specific to Lifting Installations
Project: Design of a Bar Structure with Hinges and Rigid Nodes
teaching_methods: Methods for Developing Analytical, Innovative and Critical Thinking
Study of Curricular Documents and Bibliography
Individual work, following calculation models explained in lectures and at the beginning of each lab
assessment_rules: The minimum knowledge required to pass the discipline includes: knowledge of structural design bases and the ability to perform analytical and numerical calculation of a structure. Credits are awarded if a minimum final grade of 5 is obtained. The final grade is composed of the exam grade (1/2), the laboratory grade (1/4), and the project grade (1/4).
